query: What open-response signals predict low learning satisfaction?

per_column.name: technical_issues
per_column.rationale: Binary flag extracted from open response indicating technical problems; lies outside the satisfaction score and plausibly correlates with lower satisfaction.

per_column.name: isolation_disconnection
per_column.rationale: Themed complaint signal about isolation; a legitimate external feature carrying predictive signal without restating the focus.

per_column.name: hands_on_learning_missing
per_column.rationale: Content-based flag for missing hands-on learning; distinct from the outcome and plausibly predictive.

per_column.name: engagement_complaints
per_column.rationale: Extracted engagement-complaint signal; external predictor with plausible link to satisfaction.

per_column.name: instruction_quality_gaps
per_column.rationale: Flag for instruction quality issues; a genuine predictor not derived from the score itself.

per_column.name: young_learner_struggle
per_column.rationale: Theme about young learners struggling; external signal that may predict satisfaction.

per_column.name: parent_stress_burden
per_column.rationale: Parent-stress theme extracted from text; plausible predictor outside the focus variable.

per_column.name: subject_specific_hardship
per_column.rationale: Subject-difficulty signal from open response; legitimate external feature.

per_column.name: negative_signals_count
per_column.rationale: This is a deterministic aggregate of the other negative flags; while not derived from the score itself, it is redundant with its components and is essentially a hand-built proxy for low satisfaction rather than an independent predictor. As a summed count of negative themes it borders on restating the intended target construct.

per_column.name: predicted_low_satisfaction
per_column.rationale: A column literally predicting/labelling low satisfaction is a target proxy — either derived from the focus (leakage) or a restatement of the outcome to be predicted; not a valid independent feature.

judge.rationale: Eight of the ten columns are theme-level binary flags mined from the open_response text (technical issues, isolation, missing hands-on learning, engagement complaints, instruction gaps, young-learner struggle, parent stress, subject hardship). These lie outside the satisfaction score, are not deterministic functions of it, and plausibly carry genuine predictive signal about low satisfaction — a solid set of engineered features. However, 'negative_signals_count' is a mechanical aggregate of the other flags (redundant and constructed to mirror the target), and 'predicted_low_satisfaction' is an explicit target proxy that leaks/restates the focus variable. Excluding those two, the set gives real, non-trivial predictive leverage beyond the original columns, hence moderate-to-good utility.
